subject.title: Durable Core PR 6/6: add read-only durable inspection

question: Should OpenClaw adopt an opt-in durable core with shared persisted coordination/recovery state and the associated Gateway/CLI inspection contract, or should this work remain outside core or be narrowed to existing owner-specific surfaces?
rationale: No mechanical patch can establish whether a cross-owner durable runtime, its config modes, its recovery authority, and its public inspection API belong in OpenClaw core; the related RFC and all implementation slices are still open.

options.title: Sponsor and sequence the durable core
options.body: Accept the owner-first core direction, assign ownership, and review the stack in a maintainable merge order with explicit upgrade and protocol commitments.

options.title: Narrow to existing owners
options.body: Keep task, session, subagent, and delivery diagnostics owner-specific and reject the shared durable runtime unless a concrete residual gap remains.

options.title: Keep it out of core
options.body: Decline this core architecture and invite a separately scoped external or plugin-oriented solution where current extension seams are sufficient.

recommendation.title: Sponsor and sequence the durable core
recommendation.body: Accept the owner-first core direction, assign ownership, and review the stack in a maintainable merge order with explicit upgrade and protocol commitments.

likelyOwner.reason: This contributor authored the residual-gap proposal and the complete durable-runtime stack, so they are the clearest available technical contact for the requested architectural clarification.
